label: Household Income
why_selected: Strongest demographic gradient (Part 1, 4.1). Chosen over poverty status (fpl): same signal, finer scale.

label: Age
why_selected: Added for coverage. Weaker alone, but age changes the picture at low incomes (Part 1, 4.8) and is basic to targeting.

label: Education (Highest Degree Received)
why_selected: Added for coverage. Respondent's own education; chosen over household education (HHEDUC) as it describes the person.

label: Which one of the following best describes your housing situation?
why_selected: On the shortlist. Renters and non-owners use prepaid cards far more than homeowners.

label: Primary or only employment status
why_selected: Added for coverage. Highest use among the disabled, unemployed and part-time workers.

label: Marital Status
why_selected: Added for coverage. Married respondents use prepaid cards about half as often as others.

label: Has: Checking or Savings Account at a bank or credit union
why_selected: On the shortlist. Bank-account status is the most independent strong signal (Part 1, 4.7).

label: Has: Retirement Account (such as a 401k or IRA)
why_selected: On the shortlist. Retirement account: marks attachment to mainstream long-term finance.

label: Has: Health Insurance
why_selected: Added. Health insurance: second-largest product gap after the bank account.

label: How much money do you have in savings today...?
why_selected: On the shortlist; the single strongest variable.

label: Confidence in ability to raise $2,000 in 30 days
why_selected: Added. Could raise $2,000 in 30 days: liquidity under stress. Related to savings (0.69) but far fewer missing answers.

label: Household income volatility
why_selected: Added. Month-to-month income volatility: irregular income is a stated use case for prepaid cards.

label: Number of material hardships experienced sometimes or often (0-6)
why_selected: On the shortlist. One count in place of six separate hardship items.

label: Any household member received SNAP benefits
why_selected: On the shortlist. Receipt of public benefits, which are often paid onto prepaid cards.

label: Contacted by debt collector in past 12 months
why_selected: On the shortlist. Contact from a debt collector: marker of credit distress.

label: I applied for credit and was turned down
why_selected: On the shortlist. Turned down for credit: blocked access to mainstream credit.

label: Number of financial shocks in the past year (0-11)
why_selected: On the shortlist. Number of financial shocks in the past year.

label: Knoll and Houts financial knowledge scale score
why_selected: On the shortlist. Tested financial knowledge; central to the CFPB 'unsophisticated user' question.

label: Financial well-being scale score
why_selected: Replaces the single item FWB2_3. The CFPB's own ten-item financial well-being score.

label: Past 6 months: Paid all your bills on time
why_selected: On the shortlist. Pays bills on time: the strongest money-management behaviour.
